chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Abdul Kareem ibn Amr, from Suleiman ibn Khalid who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Beware of imposing upon yourself an obligation, and then abandoning it for twelve crescents (months).'

key_terms.اثْنَيْ عَشَرَ هِلَالًا: Twelve crescents (referring to twelve lunar months)
key_terms.تُفَارِقَهَا: To separate from or abandon it
key_terms.فَرِيضَة: Obligation or duty (can be obligatory or voluntary)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the 'twelve crescents' mentioned in the hadith about consistency in worship?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises believers to be careful when setting personal religious goals or voluntary obligations, warning that abandoning them for twelve months is a sign of weakness. This teaching emphasizes the importance of consistency and persistence in worship rather than taking on more than one can sustain. In Shia scholarly tradition, this hadith is often cited to caution against 'ghuluw' (exaggeration) in voluntary acts, encouraging sustainable piety over fleeting intensity.
